title: Why the 1998 Nintendo 64 Cartridge Was Not a 'Hard‑Drive'?

scenes.text: The Nintendo 64 used 64 MB cartridges for its biggest titles.
People often say those cartridges functioned like tiny hard‑drives.
scenes.label: Cartridge = hard‑drive

scenes.text: Cartridges are ROM chips with no moving parts; they store data permanently, unlike magnetic hard‑drives which read/write dynamically.
scenes.label: ROM, not HDD
scenes.query: difference ROM cartridge vs hard drive

scenes.text: Remember: ROM means read‑only – no rewrites on the fly.
scenes.label: Read‑Only Memory
scenes.sub: Cartridges can’t save new data without extra battery backup.

scenes.text: Follow if tech moves faster than you can keep up.

description: Big N64 cartridges hold lots of data, but they’re not miniature hard‑drives. Learn the real difference between ROM and HDD. Follow for more retro tech revelations.
